The latest official applicant total and offer total are published on separate Johns Hopkins pages, while this schema permits only one source URL for acceptanceRate; no single official source reviewed states both values or a university-wide percentage.

requiredSubjects.value: No binding secondary-school subject list; four years each of English, mathematics, foreign language, laboratory science, and history/social science recommended
requiredSubjects.quote:
We do not have an official language requirement. In general, we recommend students take four years of each of the following subjects: English, mathematics, foreign language, science with laboratory, history/social science.
Please note these are only recommendations and not requirements.

admissionsTest.value: SAT or ACT required for first-year admission
admissionsTest.quote: Johns Hopkins University requires first-year applicants to submit SAT (Math and Evidence-Based Reading and Writing sections) or ACT (Math, Reading, and English sections) scores to be considered for admission.

languageRequirement.value: English test recommended for applicants whose primary language is not English or who have not attended an English-language school for the last three years; competitive scores published
languageRequirement.quote:
TOEFL, IELTS, the Duolingo English Test (DET), or the Cambridge English Exam are recommended if your primary language is not English, or you have not attended an English language school for the last three years.
TOEFL (iBT)- A minimum of 100 total
IELTS- A score of 7.0 or higher on each band
DET- A composite score of 120 or higher
Cambridge English Exam- C1 Advanced or C2 Proficiency with a Cambridge English score of 185 or higher

interview.value: No admissions interview
interview.quote: No, we do not offer interviews as part of our admissions process and are unable to grant meeting requests.

restrictedEntry.value: Only limited-enrolment major; must be listed as first-choice major and admission depends on credentials and available space
restrictedEntry.quote:
To be considered for the program, you must indicate BME as your first-choice major on your application.
Students are admitted to BME based on evaluation of credentials and space available.
Our BME major is the only limited enrollment major at Hopkins with a goal of enrolling 100–120 new first-year students each year.

applicationRoute.value: Common Application or Coalition on Scoir; Early Decision I deadline 1 November; Early Decision II and Regular Decision deadline 2 January
applicationRoute.quote:

Early Decision I Nov. 1

Regular Decision Jan. 2

omitted.reason: Johns Hopkins publishes no minimum school grade, GPA, A-level, IB, or equivalent headline offer for first-year admission; its official pages describe holistic review.
The official first-year admissions and programme pages reviewed do not state that prior work experience is required or expected for admission.
Johns Hopkins explicitly states that it does not release a separate Biomedical Engineering acceptance rate or historical data; no official course-level percentage is available.

admissionsTest.value: Test-optional; ACT or SAT not required
admissionsTest.quote: Northwestern follows a test-optional policy and will not require ACT or SAT scores from first-year or transfer candidates.

languageRequirement.value: English-proficiency score required if English is not the first/primary language or secondary schooling was not in English; DET, IELTS, or TOEFL accepted with no minimum score
languageRequirement.quote:
An English proficiency score is required for applicants whose first/primary language is not English or whose secondary schooling has not been in English.
Northwestern accepts official results from the following exams: Duolingo English Test (DET); IELTS, including IELTS Indicator; TOEFL iBT.
While there is no minimum score required by Northwestern, competitive applicants demonstrate a high level of English proficiency.

interview.value: Optional InitialView interview for international applicants; no disadvantage for not interviewing
interview.quote: Interviews are an optional addition to your application for admission and are conducted through InitialView. Applicants who are unable to or choose not to interview are not at a disadvantage in the admission process.

restrictedEntry.value: Applicants select one of six undergraduate schools; schools use the same review criteria and are not restrictive
restrictedEntry.quote: Northwestern requires all applicants to apply to one of the six undergraduate schools. There is no strategic advantage to applying to any specific school, as we use the same admission review criteria for all Northwestern undergraduate applicants. The undergraduate schools are not restrictive.

restrictedEntry.value: Students enter with a Common Year and may begin declaring a major after Spring Quarter; some majors may require consultation or formal acceptance

At the close of Spring Quarter, first-year students may begin declaring any major programs of study in the my.UChicago portal, though they will be able to add, modify, or remove majors during subsequent years.
Some majors may require consultation with the academic department or formal acceptance following completion of an application process in order to officially declare.

languageRequirement.value: Required with under 3 years of English-medium instruction: TOEFL, IELTS, or Duolingo; competitive scores are revised TOEFL iBT 5+ in every section, previous TOEFL above 100 with sub-scores above 24, IELTS 7.5+, or DET 135+
languageRequirement.quote:
If all of your high school/secondary school education was completed in English, you are considered proficient and do not need to satisfy this requirement. However, if you've completed all or some high school or secondary school in a country where English was not the language of instruction, you will be required to demonstrate English proficiency if you have had less than 3 years of instruction in English. To demonstrate English language proficiency, students are required to take the Test of English as a Foreign Language (TOEFL), the International English Language Testing Service (IELTS), or the Duolingo English Test.
We look for competitive English proficiency scores, including a TOEFL iBT score of 5 or higher (with sub-scores of 5 or higher) on the revised scale (effective January 21, 2026), or above 100 (with sub-scores above 24) on the previous 120-point scale, as well as 7.5 or above on the IELTS or 135 or higher on the Duolingo English Test (DET).

requiredSubjects.value: 15 A-G courses, including 2 years history/social science, 4 English, 3 mathematics, 2 laboratory science, 2 language other than English, 1 visual/performing arts, and 1 college-preparatory elective; at least 11 before the final school year
requiredSubjects.quote:
You must complete 15 A-G courses with at least 11 courses finished prior to the beginning of your last year of high school.
2 years history/social science
4 years of college-preparatory English
3 years of mathematics (4 years recommended)
2 years of laboratory science (3 years recommended)
2 years of language other than English (3 years recommended)
1 year of visual and performing arts (if available)
1 year of college-preparatory elective

admissionsTest.value: SAT and ACT not considered for admission or scholarships
admissionsTest.quote: UCLA will not consider SAT or ACT scores for admission or scholarship purposes.

languageRequirement.value: Required with under 3 years of English-medium instruction: TOEFL, IELTS, or Duolingo; competitive scores are revised TOEFL iBT 5+ in every section, previous TOEFL above 100 with sub-scores above 24, IELTS 7.5+, or DET 135+
languageRequirement.quote:
If all of your high school/secondary school education was completed in English, you are considered proficient and do not need to satisfy this requirement. However, if you've completed all or some high school or secondary school in a country where English was not the language of instruction, you will be required to demonstrate English proficiency if you have had less than 3 years of instruction in English. To demonstrate English language proficiency, students are required to take the Test of English as a Foreign Language (TOEFL), the International English Language Testing Service (IELTS), or the Duolingo English Test.
We look for competitive English proficiency scores, including a TOEFL iBT score of 5 or higher (with sub-scores of 5 or higher) on the revised scale (effective January 21, 2026), or above 100 (with sub-scores above 24) on the previous 120-point scale, as well as 7.5 or above on the IELTS or 135 or higher on the Duolingo English Test (DET).

interview.value: No admission interviews
interview.quote: We do not offer admission interviews. Applicants are considered for admission based upon the information they submit in the UC application.

languageRequirement.value: Required for applicants whose second language is English; accepted tests include TOEFL, IELTS, ECPE, CAE/CPE, PTE Academic, and MET, with published passing ranges
languageRequirement.quote:

MET: 64 with section scores of 59+ (4-skill MET-digital)

We require at least a 7.5 overall band score on either the paper-based or computer-delivered Academic Examination.
For exams taken before Jan. 21, 2026: We require at least a 102 overall score.
For exams taken on or after Jan. 21, 2026: We require at least a 5 in the overall score.
We require at least an 11 overall band score.
We require at least a 135 overall score.
We require at least a 191 overall score.

languageRequirement.value: Required if native language is not English: IELTS 7.5 overall; TOEFL iBT 102 before 21 January 2026 or 5 on revised scale; TOEFL Essentials 11; DET 135; Cambridge English 191
languageRequirement.quote:

We require at least a 7.5 overall band score on either the paper-based or computer-delivered Academic Examination.

university: The University of Texas at Austin

admissionsTest.value: At least one official SAT or ACT score required; SAT Essay, ACT Writing, ACT Science, and SAT Subject Tests not required
admissionsTest.quote:
Send at least one official SAT or ACT score directly from the testing agency.
We do not require the SAT Essay, ACT Writing scores, the ACT Science section, or SAT Subject Tests.

languageRequirement.value: For applicable international applicants: TOEFL 79 on the 120 scale or 4 on the 6-point scale, IELTS Academic 6.5 overall, or DET 115; exemptions apply for specified countries or qualifying schooling
languageRequirement.quote:
International applicants must submit either an official Test of English as a Foreign Language (TOEFL), International English Language Testing System (IELTS) or Duolingo English Test (DET) demonstrating an adequate knowledge of English.
International applicants are exempt from this requirement if they:
Are from a qualifying country, or
Graduate from a high school in the United States or a qualifying country after completing at least three years of study.
Minimum scores acceptable for admission are:
TOEFL: 79 (120 scale) or 4 (6-point scale) internet-based test
IELTS: An overall band of 6.5 on the Academic Examination
DET: 115 minimum overall score

interview.value: No interview for general admission
interview.quote:
Does UT Austin conduct interviews for admissions?
No, UT Austin does not provide interviews for general admission.

workExperience.value: Not required; an optional resume may include student employment
workExperience.quote:
The optional items below are NOT required for admission consideration.
Resume
You may submit a resume offering additional information about your achievements, activities, leadership positions and student employment.

restrictedEntry.value: Admission and major selection are reviewed together; first-choice major is considered holistically and second-choice consideration is limited
restrictedEntry.quote:
Each application receives an individualized holistic review as part of our decision review process. This process informs decisions of admission as well as major selection.
We consider every application individually and in relation to the admission factors for the University and for the college, school and majors to which you apply.
Competitiveness of the major you applied to

International applicants are exempt from this requirement if they:
Are from a qualifying country, or
Graduate from a high school in the United States or a qualifying country after completing at least three years of study.
Minimum scores acceptable for admission are:
TOEFL: 79 (120 scale) or 4 (6-point scale) internet-based test
IELTS: An overall band of 6.5 on the Academic Examination
DET: 115 minimum overall score

gradeRequirement.value: Minimum A-G GPA: 3.0 for California residents or 3.4 for non-California residents, including international applicants; no grade below C
gradeRequirement.quote:
To be eligible for admission to UC San Diego, you must earn the following minimum GPA in all A-G courses.
California residents must earn a GPA of 3.0 (or better) with no grade lower than "C."
Non-California residents, including International applicants, must earn a GPA of 3.4 (or better) with no grade lower than a "C."

requiredSubjects.value: Fifteen A-G college-preparatory courses: two history/social science, four English, three mathematics (four recommended), two laboratory science (three recommended), two language other than English (three recommended), one visual and performing arts, and one college-preparatory elective; at least 11 completed before senior year; grade C or better
requiredSubjects.quote:
To be eligible for admission to UC San Diego, you must complete UC College preparatory courses (A-G courses) in the subjects below and earn a "C" grade or better. Complete at least 11 of the 15 courses before your senior year of high school.
a. History/social science | 2
b. English | 4
c. Mathematics | 3 (4 recommended)
d. Laboratory science | 2 (3 recommended)
e. Language other than English (or other second language) | 2 (3 recommended)
f. Visual and performing arts | 1
g. College preparatory elective | 1

admissionsTest.value: SAT and ACT scores are not considered in admission or scholarship decisions
admissionsTest.quote: UC San Diego does not consider SAT or ACT test scores as a factor in admissions or scholarship decisions. If you choose to submit test scores, they may be used as an alternative method of fulfilling minimum requirements or for course placement should you be admitted, and enroll at the university.

languageRequirement.value: If the applicant's native language is not English and schooling was in a country where English is not the language of instruction: TOEFL 4.5 (or 83 for tests before January 2026), IELTS 7, or DET 115
languageRequirement.quote:
Demonstration of English proficiency is required if your native language is not English and your secondary/high school education was in a country where English is not the language of instruction.
Test of English as a Foreign Language (TOEFL) | 4.5 or better (Internet-based test) or 83 or higher (internet-based tests completed prior to January 2026)
International English Language Testing System (IELTS) | 7
Duolingo English Test (DET) | 115

restrictedEntry.value: Selective major with limited enrolment; applicants should name a non-selective alternate major
restrictedEntry.quote:
A selective major is one with limited enrollment, due to capacity.
Data Science
Engineering
Public Health
If you are applying to a selective major, we strongly recommend that you indicate an alternate non-selective major on your UC application. If you are not admitted to your first-choice selective major, you may be admitted to your alternate major if space is available.

requiredSubjects.value: Fifteen A-G college-preparatory courses: two history/social science, four English, three mathematics (four recommended), two laboratory science (three recommended), two language other than English (three recommended), one visual and performing arts, and one college-preparatory elective; at least 11 completed before senior year; grade C or better
requiredSubjects.quote:

requiredSubjects.value: For U.S.-system high schools: four units each of English, mathematics, and science; three social science; two foreign language, American Sign Language, or computer science; non-U.S. curricula must be deemed equivalent
requiredSubjects.quote:
The University System of Georgia (USG) requires minimum academic courses of all first-time students graduating from high school within a U.S. system of education, though most applicants exceed these in at least one area. Students graduating from a high school outside of the U.S. system of education must complete a high school curriculum deemed equivalent to a U.S. required high school curriculum by USG institutions and/or NACES-approved credential evaluator.
USG requirements include:
English - 4 Units
Math - 4 Units
Science - 4 Units
Social Science - 3 Units
Foreign Language or American Sign Language or Computer Science - 2 Units

admissionsTest.value: SAT or ACT required
admissionsTest.quote:
All first-year applicants must submit results from at least one SAT and/or ACT in order to be considered for admission.
In order to complete your application, you must submit either an SAT or ACT test score. We do not require the ACT writing section or the SAT optional essay.

languageRequirement.value: International applicants must demonstrate English proficiency using a USG-approved method; minimums include TOEFL iBT 3.5 (69 before 2026), IELTS Academic 6, SAT EBRW 480, ACT English 17, Cambridge English 169, or PTE Academic 53
languageRequirement.quote:
English language proficiency can be met by utilizing one of the approved methods listed below.
TOEFL iBT (includes Home Edition & My Best) | 3.5 (69 if taken prior to 2026)
IELTS Academic (including IELTS Online and One Skill Retake) | 6
SAT Evidence-Based Reading and Writing Section Score | 480
ACT English | 17
Cambridge English Scale Score | 169
Pearson (PTE) Academic (conventional and online) | 53

interview.value: Optional third-party unscripted interview for non-native English speakers; no alumni or admission-staff interviews
interview.quote:
Applicants who are non-native English speakers have the option to participate in a third-party, unscripted interview.
We do not conduct alumni or admission staff interviews.
While an interview is optional, there are certain language proficiency requirements international applicants must complete to be considered for first-year admission.

restrictedEntry.value: First-year applicants do not apply to a specific major or college, but intended major and evidence of preparation are considered in review
restrictedEntry.quote: When you apply to Georgia Tech as a first-year applicant, you do not apply to a specific major or college. However, on your Common Application, you are asked to select an intended (primary) major and may select an additional major of interest (secondary). We ask you to do this because consideration of your major is an important part of our application review process, as we seek to ensure an academically diverse first-year class.
